clusterDetail: Said together as /{ipa}/. The whole cluster takes the class of its first letter {head} → {cls|lower}.
leadingDetail: The first letter {head} decides the class → {cls|lower}.
vowelShape: The vowel changes shape before a final
finalChanged: As an initial {ch} is /{initial}/, but as a final it becomes /{final}/. Thai has only 8 final sounds: k t p m n ŋ j w.
finalSame: {ch} keeps its /{sound}/ sound as a final.
liveSpecial: The vowel {vowel} carries its own final /{sound}/, so it is always live.
liveFinal: Ends in the sonorant /{sound}/ → live (can be prolonged).
deadFinal: Ends in the stop /{sound}/ → dead (cut off abruptly).
liveOpen: Long vowel with no final → live.
deadOpen: Short vowel with no final → dead (ends in a glottal stop /ʔ/).
wCluster: {ch} + /ua/ doesn’t occur in Thai (the ว in the cluster already gives /w/).
noClosed: This vowel doesn’t take a final, so the final is ignored.
noFinal: {ch} is not used as a final consonant.
excluded: This vowel can’t take final {ch} (the sound /aw/ is written เ-า).
tri: Mai tri (๊) always gives the high tone.
chattawa: Mai chattawa (๋) always gives the rising tone.
triRare: In standard spelling ๊ only goes on mid-class consonants; elsewhere only in loanwords/onomatopoeia.
chattawaRare: In standard spelling ๋ only goes on mid-class consonants.
ekLow: Low class + mai ek (่) → falling tone.
thoLow: Low class + mai tho (้) → high tone.
liveHigh: High class + live, no mark → rising tone.
liveOther: {cls} class + live, no mark → mid tone.
deadLowShort: Low class + dead, short vowel → high tone.
deadLowLong: Low class + dead, long vowel → falling tone.
